title: Partner Co-sell: Pipeline Review - Constellation Partners
summary: Regular partner pipeline review to align on co-sell opportunities. Reviewed three active deals (pilot, mid-market, enterprise), discussed technical blockers (VPC peering, KMS, data residency), and agreed on next steps: send joint pipeline spreadsheet, schedule exec intro, run a benchmark pilot in July.
action_items: Maya Thompson - Send joint pipeline spreadsheet + updated ROI sheet - due 2026-06-17
Liam O'Rourke - Draft pilot benchmark plan (latency, throughput, dataset, success criteria) - due 2026-06-22
Rachel Kim - Share list of targeted accounts for 2Q co-sell push and intro to internal AE - due 2026-06-18
Priya Singh - Confirm procurement timeline for Enterprise deal (legal/compliance steps) - due 2026-06-21
next_steps: Redwood to share co-sell deck and pipeline spreadsheet
Schedule exec sponsor intro between Maya and Constellation's Head of Partnerships
Agree pilot scope and kick-off in first week of July
Set up technical deep dive / VPC design session with Daniel and Redwood infra team
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rachel (Constellation VP Partnerships), Daniel (Head of Cloud), Priya (Sales Ops)

Summary: Quick pipeline sync to surface co-sell motion opportunities and remove blockers for two priority deals. Lots of back-and-forth on hosting options (hosted vs dedicated), security requirements, and an ask to run a benchmark pilot in July.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time today. Rachel, thanks for coordinating on your side. Quick round-robin, and then we'll jump into the pipeline spreadsheet.

[00:18] Rachel (Constellation): Yeah no problem, thanks Maya, hi all. We, um, want to get aligned on which deals you want to co-sell and what the handoffs look like.

[00:28] Maya: Perfect. Liam from our side will cover the technical ask — especially VPC/KMS stuff Daniel flagged last week. Liam?

[00:34] Liam (Redwood SE): Yeah hi all. I'll keep it high level for the first pass but we do need to map out network requirements early, especially for the enterprise account. VPC peering or PrivateLink, SAML SSO for user access, and KMS/HSM for key management.

[00:50] Daniel (Constellation): Right, so for the enterprise customer they require customer-managed keys and audit logs, and they want data residency in EU. Is that supported by Redwood?

[00:59] Maya: Yes we support KMS integrations and region pinning; for the VPC side we have Private deployments that can be customer-managed. There are different tradeoffs between hosted and Dedicated — Liam can detail latency and cost implications.

[01:18] Liam: Quick note on that — Dedicated or Private will give you more control and easier KMS integration, but cost per token and unit economics will change. For high throughput the Dedicated pool is usually the sweet spot; hosted is faster to start but you get limited guarantees.

[01:36] Priya (Constellation): Cost is a big one for our channel customers; if we push Redwood as a co-sell option, what level of discount/partner pricing do we expect?

[01:45] Maya: We have partner pricing tiers; I'll put the specifics in the spreadsheet but typical co-sell deals get partner discounts plus joint pipeline credit if you bring qualified leads. We'll follow up in the next email.

[01:54] Rachel: Great. Can we go through the three deals we flagged last week? Quick status on each?

[02:02] Maya: Sure — Deal A is the mid-market pilot with FinServe (name obfuscated), they're interested in a POC for customer support summarization. Rachel you introduced last month — status?

[02:12] Rachel: They're still in procurement; they want a 30-day pilot, have logged some security concerns but seem motivated.

[02:20] Liam: For Deal A pilot we recommend hosted with prefix caching and small quantization to keep costs low, target latency under 350ms p95, throughput about 20 rps. If we can meet that, conversion is likely.

[02:35] Daniel: 350ms p95 — that's tight on a shared host for multi-tenant; do you think Dedicated would be needed?

[02:41] Liam: Not necessarily for the pilot — but for production at scale yes. Pilot can be hosted to prove functionality; if they need stricter SLOs we can shift to Dedicated.

[02:52] Maya: Deal B is the enterprise opportunity with Helios Corp — this is the one with the KMS and data residency asks Daniel mentioned. They also asked for SOC 2 evidence and an audit log delivery.

[03:05] Daniel: On their side they want private endpoints and a way to rotate keys via their HSM. Is Redwood able to do HSM integrations?

[03:12] Liam: We support KMS/HSM integrations through Redwood Private; you'll need to run a private control plane or have a VPC peering setup. There is a bit of engineering work but it's a supported pattern.

[03:23] Priya: How long does that usually take? Procurement is asking timeline estimates.

[03:29] Maya: For technical delivery I'd say 4-8 weeks for a basic Private setup including KMS integration, depending on their networking team availability. We'll provide a more exact timeline once we scope the network design with Daniel.

[03:42] Rachel: Ok — that's doable, their procurement cycle is about six weeks so it lines up if we move fast.

[03:47] Maya: Deal C is a smaller web app integration they want for search relevance — lower ARPU but high volume. Good for showcasing cost efficiency.

[03:55] Rachel: For that one we can go hosted and try to spin quickly. It might be a good test case for co-marketing.

[04:02] Maya: Agreed. Now — a few asks from Constellation: 1) A pilot benchmark plan with success criteria, 2) an updated pipeline sheet we can both own, 3) an intro to Redwood's sales leadership for the enterprise motion.

[04:14] Rachel: Yes, and we'd like a short co-sell deck to share internally — positioning, partner benefits and sample pricing.

[04:20] Maya: We'll share that. I'll also add expected partner discounts and co-sell credit terms.

[04:27] (brief crosstalk)

[04:30] Liam: On the benchmark plan — propose we measure p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, and a model quality check with a small evaluation set. We'll need access to a sanitized data sample for the customer.

[04:44] Daniel: For the enterprise customer we can provide a scrubbed dataset, but we need to confirm where logs land and how long they're retained. It's a compliance question.

[04:52] Maya: Redwood's hosted API has configurable retention; Private deployments can be set to never persist logs if that's required. We'll put specifics in the security docs.

[05:02] Priya: Speaking of security docs, can you send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and any third-party attestation we can share with our procurement team?

[05:09] Maya: Yes I'll attach those. Also will share our standard security FAQ for partners.

[05:15] Rachel: Quick question — what's the typical co-sell credit model? Is it deal registration or lead share?

[05:21] Maya: We do both. For inbound registered leads you get partner credits and dedicated AE support; for joint sourced deals we have an attribution model in the partner portal. Again I'll include details in the spreadsheet.

[05:31] Daniel: Any concerns about competitors? I know some of our customers evaluate OpenAI with hosted endpoints and VertexAI on GCP. How does Redwood compete?

[05:39] Liam: Strengths are inference economics and flexible deployment — we can run in customer's cloud or private, and our batching/caching optimizations reduce cost. In many cases we beat broad hosted providers on total cost while preserving model quality. But for pure turn-key model access some customers still use larger cloud vendors; it's about the tradeoff between control and speed to value.

[05:58] Priya: Ok useful. Let's talk timing: Pilot in first week of July — does that work for Redwood?

[06:04] Maya: Yes, we can kick off a pilot the week of July 6th. Liam will own technical setup and we'll need Constellation to provide account contacts and a scrubbed sample data set.

[06:12] Rachel: I'll coordinate introductions to the customer AEs and procurement.

[06:18] Maya: Great. Any deeper technical concerns before we move on?

[06:23] Daniel: One more — network architecture. For Private deployment do you prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink? Our security team favors PrivateLink.

[06:31] Liam: We support both. PrivateLink is usually cleaner for firewalling but has some regional availability nuances; we'll propose the diagram and both options in the design session.

[06:41] (silence, note-taking)

[06:45] Maya: Ok shifting gears — marketing and co-sell GTM. Rachel, what's Constellation's appetite for joint webinars or case studies?

[06:52] Rachel: We can do a webinar for the smaller deals in August, case study post-launch for the enterprise one. We prefer content that highlights integration and cost savings.

[07:01] Maya: We'll prepare a joint tweet/thread and a one-pager. Also happy to run a joint demo with your AEs.

[07:07] Priya: For leads generated from co-marketing, what's the routing process?

[07:12] Maya: We'll route them into the partner portal and assign to either Redwood AE or your AE based on lead type; we'll confirm in the pipeline sheet.

[07:20] Rachel: Sounds good. Any legal hurdles we should prep for Helios Corp? They insist on liability limits and data processing addendums.

[07:28] Maya: We'll share a standard mutual NDA and DPA. For liability caps we'll need Redwood legal to review if they ask for enterprise-level amendments — that may extend the timeline. We'll flag that in the deal notes.

[07:40] (transition)

[07:42] Liam: Back to pilot scoping — propose success criteria: 1) p95 latency < 400ms, 2) model accuracy metric above baseline by X% (we'll define), 3) cost projection within the quoted budget. We'll put concrete numbers in the benchmark doc.

[07:58] Daniel: We'll work with your SE to define the evaluation set. Also need to ensure keys never leave our HSM in production; for pilot hosted maybe we can use a temporary KMS token.

[08:08] Liam: That's feasible — temporary tokens for pilot, full KMS for production. We'll document the process.

[08:15] Maya: Alright, time check — about 12 minutes in. Anything else from Constellation side?

[08:21] Priya: Procurement wants estimated ARR and contract terms for Deal B to present to finance. Can you provide topline pricing?

[08:28] Maya: I'll include a pricing ballpark in the pipeline sheet and mark it as estimate. For firm pricing we'll need to lock in model usage patterns.

[08:37] Rachel: On the pipeline sheet, can you add columns for "co-sell owner", "commit date", and "legal risk"? That would help us prioritize.

[08:45] Maya: Absolutely. We'll add those and share a Google sheet with edit access.

[08:50] (brief pause)

[08:52] Liam: Quick question about monitoring — do you need token-level cost breakdowns for your customers? We can expose per-route metrics in the console and set alerts.

[09:02] Daniel: Yes that will help downstream teams. We'd like to set thresholds so we can auto-scale or throttle.

[09:09] Liam: We have autoscaling policies and rate-limit hooks; we'll include recommended settings.

[09:16] Maya: Ok folks, let's recap next steps — Maya to share pipeline and co-sell deck; Liam to send benchmark plan; Rachel to share intro list and targeted accounts; Priya to confirm procurement timeline. We'll sync next week for the exec intro.

[09:34] Rachel: Sounds good. One last thing — is there a standard partner agreement we can preview?

[09:40] Maya: Yes, I'll attach the partner agreement and DPA. Legal point: enterprise addenda can take longer, we'll flag early.

[09:48] (small talk)

[09:52] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with the pipeline sheet.

[09:56] Priya: Thanks all.

[09:58] Daniel: Thanks.

[10:00] (meeting end)

Notes: Transcript contains some informal tagging and occasional transcription errors; speaker labels approximate. Refer to attached docs: /links/partner-pipeline-2026-06-15.xlsx, /links/security-pack.pdf, /links/partner-deck.pdf
